paper.title: Causal Bandits: The Pareto Optimal Frontier of Adaptivity, a Reduction to Linear Bandits, and Limitations around Unknown Marginals

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit with post-action contexts, conditionally benign environments (known marginals)
unmapped: after acting, the learner observes a post-action context Z in a finite set of size |Z| in addition to the reward
conditionally benign: the conditional distribution of Y given Z does not depend on the action (Z d-separates action and reward)
the learner knows the marginal distributions nu_a(Z) of the post-action context for each action
settings.definition_quote: An environment $\env\in\envspace$ is \textit{conditionally benign} if and only if there exists $p\in\cP(\contextspace\times\rewardspace)$ such that for each $a\in\actionspace$, $\env_a(Z)\ll p(Z)$ and $\env_a(Y|Z)=p(Y|Z)$ p-a.s.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit with post-action contexts, arbitrary environments (known marginals)
unmapped: after acting, the learner observes a post-action context Z in a finite set of size |Z|; no conditional-benign structure assumed (any environment in P(Z x Y)^A)
the learner is given the marginal distributions nu_a(Z) of the post-action context
settings.definition_quote: For each round $t\in[T]$, the learner picks an action $A_t$ from $\actionspace$ and then receives a context-reward pair $(Z_t, Y_t)$ which is independently sampled from $\env_{A_t}\in\cP(\contextspace\times\rewardspace)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Conditionally benign environments, algorithms agnostic to marginals (lower bound)
unmapped: post-action context Z observed after acting; conditionally benign environment
the learner does NOT know the marginals of the post-action contexts (algorithm constant in q)
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm $\alg$ is said to be \emph{agnostic to marginals} if, for any $\actionspace,\contextspace$ and $T$, the map $q \mapsto \alg(\actionspace,\contextspace,T, q)$ is constant over $\cP(\contextspace)^{\actionspace}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Conditionally benign environments with epsilon-close approximate marginals
unmapped: post-action context Z observed after acting; conditionally benign environment
the learner is given approximate marginals tilde nu(Z) that are epsilon-close (sup_a L1 distance <= epsilon) to the true ones
settings.definition_quote: For any $\varepsilon\geq0$, $\tilde\env(Z)$ and $\env(Z)$ are said to be $\varepsilon$-close if $\sup_{a\in\actionspace}\sum_{z\in\contextspace}\lrabs{\tilde\env_a(z)-\env_a(z)}\leq\varepsilon.$

algorithms.name: Dynamic balancing (DB) with two base learners (benign + arbitrary)
requires_knowledge_of: marginals of post-action contexts (via base learner)

symbols.R: worst-case expected regret bound of the algorithm over all environments

conditions: algorithm satisfies sup over all environments of E[Reg(T)] <= R(T; A, Z)

source.label: lower bound: pareto lower bound
source.quote: There exists constants $c, c'>0$ such that, for all MAB algorithms $\alg$, rate functions $R(T;\actionspace,\contextspace)$, if, for all $\actionspace,\contextspace, T$ $\sup_{\env} \E_{\env,\alg}[\Reg(T)]\leq R(T;\actionspace,\contextspace)$, then ... either $R(T;\actionspace,\contextspace)>c'T$, or there exists a conditionally benign environment $\env$ such that $\E_{\env,\alg}[\Reg(T)]\geq c\cdot \frac{|\actionspace|T}{R(T;\actionspace,\contextspace)}.$

results.notes: Generalizes Bilodeau et al. Theorem 6.2. Learner may know marginals.

source.label: regret bound: phased elimination w-c eps=0
source.quote: For all $\delta\in(0,1)$, the policy $\elim(\delta)$ ... satisfies ... for all conditionally benign environments $\env$, $\Reg(t)\leq C\sqrt{\dimspan{\env} \log\lr{\frac{|\actionspace|\log T}{\delta}}t}, \forall t\in[T]$ with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Holds for all t in [T]; written at t=T. Regret is realized pseudo-regret (via means). Corollary 4.2 (PE is d-benign) follows.

source.label: regret bound: phased elimination w-c eps=0
source.quote: In particular, after taking $\delta=1/T$, we obtain the expected regret bound $\hE_{\env,\elim(\delta)}[\Reg(T)]=O\lr{\sqrt{\dimspan{\env}T\log(|\actionspace|T)}}.$

source.label: regret bound: phased elimination gap-dependent eps=0
source.quote: For all $\delta\in(0,1)$, the policy $\elim(\delta)$ ... satisfies the following regret for all conditionally benign environments $\env$, $\Reg(T)\leq C\cdot\frac{\dimspan{\env}\log\lr{|\actionspace|\log T/\delta}}{\mingap(\env)}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Paper notes this is also new for stochastic linear bandits with finite action sets.

source.quote: For all $\actionspace, \contextspace, T\geq|\actionspace|$ and MAB algorithms $\alg\in\noncausalspace$, there exists a conditionally benign environment $\env\in\envspace$ such that $\E_{\env,\alg}[\Reg(T)]\geq c\sqrt{|\actionspace|T}$, where $c>0$ is a universal constant.

source.label: regret bound: phased elimination w-c general eps
source.quote: In any conditionally environment $\env$ suppose we instantiate $\elim(\delta)$ with $\tilde\env(Z)$. If $\tilde\env(Z)$ and $\env(Z)$ are $\varepsilon-$close, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of $\elim(\delta)$ is bounded for all rounds $t\in[T]$ by $\Reg(t)\leq C\lr{\sqrt{\dimspan{\tilde\env} \log\lr{\frac{|\actionspace|\log T}{\delta}}t}+\varepsilon t\sqrt{\dimspan{\tilde\env}}\log T}$

results.notes: Holds for all t in [T]; written at t=T.

source.label: regret bound: C-UCB
source.quote: In any conditionally benign environment $\env$, the regret of $\cucb(\delta)$ is bounded by $\Reg(t) = O \lr{\sqrt{\log(|\contextspace|T/\delta)}\lr{\sqrt{|\contextspace|}+\sqrt{\log(T/\delta')}}\sqrt{t}}$ for all $t\in[T]$, conditioning on event ... which happens with probability at least $1-\delta-\delta'$.

results.notes: Anytime over t in [T] (written at T), probability 1-delta-delta'; with delta'=delta gives Prop 3.4. Paper says this anytime C-UCB bound is new.

conditions: specific algorithm: Phased Elimination (Alg. 2) modified to always choose an exact G-optimal design
there exists a non-benign environment with Delta_min = Delta for any Delta in (0,1)

source.label: fact: phased elimination incurs linear regret in some non-benign settings
source.quote: Suppose we modify \cref{alg: phased-elimination} such that, in each phase, we always choose an exact-optimal design whenever feasible. For any $\actionspace,\contextspace$ and $T$ with $|\actionspace|>|\contextspace|\geq 3$ and $\Delta\in(0,1)$, there exists a non-benign environment $\env$ such that $\mingap(\env)=\Delta$, while \cref{alg: phased-elimination} will never play the optimal arm, hence incurring linear regret, $\Reg(t)\geq\mingap(\env)\cdot t$

results.notes: Holds for all t; written at T. Deterministic rewards in construction.

source.label: regret bound: cucb and ucb
source.quote: $\cucb$ is a $d$-benign family for $d(\delta)=O((\sqrt{|\contextspace|}+\sqrt{\log (T/\delta)})\sqrt{\log(|\contextspace|T/\delta)})$ and $\ucb$ is a $d'$-arbitrary family for $d'(\delta)= O(\sqrt{|\actionspace|\log(|\actionspace|T/\delta)})$.

results.notes: d-benign: w.p. 1-O(delta), regret <= d(delta) sqrt(t) for all t; written at T. UCB part is folklore and not recorded separately.
